newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volatilities hold firm.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volatilities hold firm.

text.p: Implied volatilities in major U.S. stock index options held mostly firm Monday as the underlying market struggled to recover from Friday's heavy selloff, traders said.
"They're starting to take volatility in, but it opened up really strong," one S&P 500 futures-options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said.

Volatilities for September S&P 500 futures-options were around 23 and for December were in the upper 22 region, up slightly from Friday, when they rose sharply on the market's decline, the trader said.
At the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the volatility index was up 0.44 at 28.58 after climbing to 29.24 intraday.
Paul Foster at Mercury Trading in Chicago said he expected volatilities to spike in early trading as investors scrambled to buy protection or speculate on the market's next move.
"All of a sudden everyone's thinking 'hedge, hedge, hedge' or 'speculate, speculate, speculate'," he said..
The trader at the CME said he expected index volatilities to remain firm through Wednesday as investors and traders factor in the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy setting meeting.
The Federal Open Market Committee meets Tuesday and few economists expect a change in rates.
Referring to volatilities, the trader said, "I think they'll start coming out Wednesday."

Bernie Schaeffer, head of the Investment Research Institute in Cincinnati, said in a report that the VIX has been on an uptrend and has not seen the type of climactic spike that has characterized the end of corrections previously.
On Friday, when the Dow 30 average .DJI dropped 247 points, the VIX reached 29.39 intraday before closing at 28.14. It closed last Thursday at 25.99.
Despite firm volatilities in stock indexes, some traders noted that investors appeared little concerned with the market's selloff, suggesting there could be more to come.
Jay Shartsis at R.F. Lafferty & Co in New York noted that the put/call ratio Friday was relatively low, with call volume outpacing put volume despite the heavy decline.
Often put volume will increase on a decline as investors scramble to buy puts to protect positions. Puts give holders the right to sell at a set price.
"It's astounding," Shartis said of the put/call ratio. "There's no fear."
By 1300 CDT/1800 GMT, put volume in S&P 100 index .OEX options led call volume by 32,484 to 25,849. In S&P 500 index .SPX options, put volume outpaced call volume 63,899 to 26,072.
Traders said turnover was on the light side and the FOMC meeting was probably keeping some investors sidelined.
But the SPX September 900 put traded a heavy 12,827 contracts. The option, which had open interest going into today of 27,466 contracts, fell 3/4 to 26-1/4.
Harrison Roth at Cowen & Co said the action was split between buyers and sellers of that particular option.
